title: Diagnose & fix blank stage after opening .fla (layers show, artwork missing)
summary: The import creates layers but the stage renders empty at the playhead frame, which points to objects being emitted onto the wrong frame index, dropped fills/paints, or transforms placing them off-stage/zero-sized. Plan: trace the .fla import path end-to-end, pin the exact drop point with a synthetic fixture test that fails before the fix, then correct frame indexing / transform / fill mapping and verify against both the synthetic fixture and a real .fla.

steps.description: Trace the import path: find where Command::ImportToStage / ImportInto is handled in crates/buzz-app/src/app.rs (search for `Command::Import` handlers), then follow into the FLA/XFL reader to see how DOMLayer → LayerStack and DOMShape/DOMInstance → buzz_scene::Object are built. Record exactly which frame index each object lands on, what transform is applied, and what Paint/FillSpec is produced.
steps.verification: grep for `ImportInto|ImportToStage` handlers in app.rs; note the function that populates Scene layers/objects.

steps.description: Write a minimal synthetic .xfl/.fla fixture (one shape on one layer at frame 1 with a solid fill and identity transform) plus a test that imports it and asserts: ≥1 object exists in the scene, `layer.objects_at(0)` is non-empty, and its bounds intersect the stage rect. This test must FAIL before any fix, proving the drop point.
files: crates/buzz-app/tests/fla_import.rs (or the crate owning the FLA reader)
steps.verification: `cargo test -p buzz-app fla` fails with objects_at(0) empty / no object — confirms diagnosis.

steps.description: Fix the identified drop point in the FLA/XFL importer: (a) correct frame indexing if XFL's 1-based frames are stored as-is while scene playback is 0-based (shift by 1 or map first keyframe to frame 0); (b) apply layer+object transforms so objects land inside stage_rect; (c) ensure solid/gradient fills produce a non-blank Paint and bitmap references fall back to a visible placeholder rather than transparent. Keep changes minimal to the importer only.
files: crates/buzz-app/src/import.rs (or whichever module holds the FLA reader)
steps.verification: `cargo test -p buzz-app fla` passes: object present at frame 0, bounds intersect stage.

steps.description: End-to-end verification with a real .fla: open it in the app (or via the same import function in an integration test if a sample file is available) and confirm the stage renders non-blank at the playhead; run full `cargo test` to check for regressions.
steps.verification: `cargo build && cargo test` clean; manual open of user's .fla shows artwork on stage.

risks: The blank stage may be caused by multiple compounding issues (frame index AND missing fills); step 3 fixes them together, so the fixture test should assert both object presence and visible paint.
If the FLA reader stores objects per-frame lazily, fixing indexing alone won't help if `objects_at` is never called for frame 0 — check Scene::find_object / Layer::objects_at usage in the renderer.
Real .fla files may use features (bitmaps, symbols) not covered by the synthetic fixture; final verification needs the user's actual file.
questions: Is a sample .fla file available (path?) that reproduces the blank stage, so step 4 can use it instead of only the synthetic fixture?
Should imported frames keep Adobe's 1-based numbering or be normalized to scene frame 0 as first?
